evals.name: scrub-typical-customer-prompt
evals.prompt: Scrub this text using known entities 'Providence Health' and 'Sarah Chen': 'Sarah Chen at Providence Health asked about $4.2M ARR and a 5,847 employee deal in #providence-deal-room. Email s.chen@providence.org, SF org id 00D5g0000XYZAbcDEF, linkedin.com/in/sarah-chen-12345, case OCC EA-2024-018.'
evals.expected_output: All 9 entities scrubbed: 1 COMPANY (Providence Health), 1 PERSON (Sarah Chen), 1 EMAIL, 1 ORG_ID, 1 REVENUE ({{REVENUE_1_ARR}}), 1 HEADCOUNT, 1 SLACK_CHANNEL, 1 LINKEDIN, 1 CASE_ID. The phrase 'employee deal' is preserved (only the number bracketed). Salesforce product names and round-bucket headcounts left alone (none present here).

evals.name: restore-with-unknown-placeholder
evals.prompt: Restore this LLM response using the map from eval 1: '{{PERSON_1}} at {{COMPANY_1}} asked about ${{REVENUE_1_ARR}} and the {{HEADCOUNT_1}} employee deal. We also discussed {{ORG_ID_99}} which I have no record of.'
evals.expected_output: Known placeholders ({{PERSON_1}}, {{COMPANY_1}}, {{REVENUE_1_ARR}}, {{HEADCOUNT_1}}) restored to real values. The unknown {{ORG_ID_99}} (which the LLM invented) left as-is and surfaced in stderr.

evals.name: whitelist-skipped
evals.prompt: Scrub: 'We're proposing Service Cloud + Agentforce for the customer's Health Cloud rollout, integrating with Microsoft Dynamics on Azure.'
evals.expected_output: Nothing scrubbed. Salesforce, Service Cloud, Agentforce, Health Cloud, Microsoft Dynamics, Azure are all in the built-in whitelist.

evals.name: round-bucket-headcount-preserved
evals.prompt: Scrub: 'A 25,000 employee enterprise vs. a 5,847 employee mid-market.'
evals.expected_output: Only 5,847 is bracketed (precise count). 25,000 is preserved (round bucket).

evals.name: no-input-error
evals.prompt: Run scrub with no --input and no stdin
evals.expected_output: Exits with error: 'no input. Pass --input <file>, ...' (the err-doctrine in action: plain-English cause + what to do).

evals.name: help-mode-no-scrub
evals.expected_output: Prints the SKILL.md walkthrough (the trick: bidirectional placeholders, when to invoke, modes, what gets scrubbed, CLI shape, library use, safety rules). Does NOT scrub anything. Does NOT prompt for input.
